## What you should be able to do tonight

- Identify a model order from an ACF and PACF pair with no reference table in front of you.
- State what your first strategy's evaluation concluded, and the one number that decided it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>35 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 64 to 69. The blind identification exercise from day 65 is the one worth doing if you skipped it; it is the fastest-decaying skill in this week.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Ten more blind identification trials with a fresh seed, then write from memory: the three stationarity conditions, the ACF and PACF signatures of AR and MA, and the difference between what AIC and BIC target.

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, tenth sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications, the sevenths, and 7 percent compounded for 10 years as a multiple, in your head.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> The counting problem that separates people: how many ways can you arrange the letters of MISSISSIPPI? Then, what fraction of those arrangements have no two S adjacent? Do the second by placing the non-S letters first.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Conditional probability with a trap: you are told one of two coins is fair and the other is two-headed. You pick one, flip it three times, and get three heads. Probability you picked the two-headed coin? Then say what the answer approaches after ten heads and why it never reaches 1.
:::
:::
